metadata.case_name: CHEUNG TZE MING v. CHAN KWOK KEUNG AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: Employed for some 20 years in a metalwork factory making small moulds for plastic flowers and the like.
plaintiff.occupation_after: He returned to work on 17th April 1979. Although his work is done sitting down the Plaintiff suffers discomfort after a time and his output has fallen.
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: He should be capable at working at most jobs in a factory till the age of 55 and 60 but would then have to reduce his work load in comparison with a healthy individual of the same age.

source: He was admitted to hospital with multiple lacerations over the face and a posterior dislocation of his left hip.

injuries.description: deviated nasal septum to the left diminishing the air passage by about 60%
source: The nasal septum is deviated to the left diminishing the air passage by about 60% but leaving a patent air passage.

injuries.description: posterior dislocation of his left hip
source: He was admitted to hospital with multiple lacerations over the face and a posterior dislocation of his left hip.

manifestations.description: Pain after sitting for any length of time
Cannot comfortably walk for more than half an hour and then only slowly
Upper end of the femur was slightly rotated clockwise
Diminished air passage in the left nostril by about 60% but leaving a patent air passage
Potential to lead to a blocking of the duct to the air sinuses; if this later leads to any real problem an operation could become necessary (Dr Wedderburn: chances not more than 1%)

treatments_received: The dislocation was reduced under general anaesthetic
Transferred to another hospital after three weeks
Discharged two weeks after cast removal
treatments_future: Possibility of future surgery to his nasal passage (Dr Wedderburn does not place the chances of such operation becoming necessary at more than 1%)
Possibility of hip replacement in the future

losses.description: Restriction of hip joint movement, pain after sitting, inability to walk comfortably for more than half an hour (and then only slowly); first signs of osteoarthritis are present and he will suffer increasing discomfort in the future.
